your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Med is already mortgaged and useless to me. If I die to Claude, he gets it and completes browns; gifting it to Gemini denies that. No liquidity possible after rejected offers, so maximize anti-leader odds.
I have no assets left and no good trade improves my win chance. Buying blockers risks Claude inheriting them if I bust; conserve $277 and hope to survive/collect Go while Gemini pressures Claude.

This is below mortgage value but maybe Gemini values cash/anti-Claude. If accepted, I have only $17 but $375 mortgage value, enough to barely survive one green and maybe create a dark-blue comeback if I reach GO.

Better than chasing both blues below mortgage. Buying Park at mortgage+25 lets me mortgage it back to retain ~$252 effective cash while splitting Gemini’s dark-blue set and blocking Claude if Gemini collapses.
Last serious attempt: Boardwalk at $275 can be mortgaged for $200, leaving me ~$202 effective cash plus a key blocker. If accepted, mortgage immediately; if rejected, stop trading.
Gemini won’t part with blues and Claude won’t help. With no assets, survival is thin, but preserving $277 is better than buying marginal mortgaged junk or funding Claude.
Stay in jail as long as possible; I own nothing and the board is lethal. Rolling is strictly better than paying $50, with only a 1/6 chance to leave and mostly safer landing spots if doubles hit.
Roll again. Paying $50 to enter a lethal board with no assets is awful; jail is my shelter. If doubles hit, hope for survivable landing/Go cycle, otherwise preserve cash.

Third jail attempt: rolling is dominated over paying because doubles save $50; if the engine forces payment after a miss, no worse than paying now. Need preserve every dollar and hope for survivable movement.
Forced to pay after three non-doubles. Cash drops to $227; no assets. Survival depends entirely on dodging Claude’s developed reds/greens/light blues and maybe passing GO.
